description: For an ILLUSTRATED STORY (Fuzzframe paints one picture per scene in one art style and a narrator tells it; the other kind, a motion film, you write as code): creates an illustrated animated short in the person's Fuzzframe account from your final script, kept word for word, and your storyboard for it (the guide's STORYBOARD) (this uses their credits: the brief's Make it is the OK in make it for me; in choose each step, picking the voice is the OK). Fuzzframe draws the pictures, records the voice and assembles the film in its studio: the person reviews the storyboard there and presses "Generate video". No film code is written for a story. Looks: vintage (Vintage editorial illustration: Warm paper, textured illustration, elegant serif type, slow cinematic movement.); handdrawn (Hand-drawn storytelling: Illustrated environments, simple characters, sketch details, gentle animation.); collage (Cinematic collage: Layered images, masking, paper and photographic textures, depth and parallax.); anime (Anime-style originals: Cel-shaded original characters, soft painted skies, cinematic framing.); noir (Ink noir: High-contrast black ink, deep shadows, one red accent.); papercut (Paper cut-out: Layered cut paper, soft shadows, handmade depth.); lamplit (Lamplit oil: Moody period scenes in oil paint, lit by one warm light.); baroque (Baroque oil: Dark cinematic oil painting: dramatic light out of deep shadow, gold highlights, epic scale.).

captions.description: Whether the story shows captions of what is said; false for none

episode.description: Its episode number in that series, so it's marked made

format.description: The frame's shape: "vertical" 9:16 (Shorts, Reels, TikTok) unless they ask for "wide" 16:9 (YouTube, a website, a presentation). Its pictures are drawn for it, so it can't change later. Left out, an episode of a series keeps the series' shape, else vertical

language.description: The language the script is written and narrated in

music_from.description: The id of another of their videos whose music this story plays (e.g. an earlier video they name). Left out, an episode of a series plays the music of the episode before; change it later with the music tool

own_look.description: The id of a look of their own, from a picture they uploaded (story_looks lists them). It wins over look; for look pass the closest one

script.description: The voiceover, one paragraph per item, exactly as it will be said

series.description: The series this story belongs to, by name (from plan_series / next_episode)

storyboard.description: Your storyboard, as the guide's STORYBOARD says: one scene per paragraph of script, in order

accent.description: One accent colour that suits the mood, as a hex code, e.g. #e8b06b

character.description: The one protagonist who lives the story and appears in most scenes, so they're drawn the same each time: build, age, clothing, colours, one distinctive detail. "" for a chronicle, a cast of many, an explanation, or an unseen narrator

environment.description: The world the story happens in and how it's treated, one sentence; each scene shows its own place in it

lighting.description: The light across the whole video, a short phrase

motifs.description: Two or three objects or shapes that can come back now and then, never a pose; "" for none

point.description: The whole story in 12 words or fewer

scenes.description: One per paragraph of the script, in the same order

camera.description: push in to a realisation, pull back to show scale, drift for time passing, tiltDown, settle, still

movement.description: calm: a quiet, tender line, long holds; lively: the story moving on (most scenes); dramatic: action, danger, a shock or the turn, fast close cuts (only the few peaks). The first scene isn't calm

on_screen.description: Up to 5 words shown on screen, copied exactly from this scene's own words, or "" (most scenes): for the hook's question and the key realisation

second_picture_at.description: Only for a scene of more than about 8 seconds whose words move to a clearly different image half way: the exact words where the second picture comes on, at the start of a sentence or clause. "" for one picture (most scenes)

transition.description: How it comes in: dissolve for continuity, cut for a jolt, slide, wipe

title.description: The video's title, at most 8 words (their own title word for word if they gave one)

world.description: The world every picture is set in: its culture or mythology, era, place, dress, architecture (e.g. "Ancient Greek mythology: classical robes and armour, marble temples, olive groves and sea"), so a name alone is never drawn in another culture

voice_id.description: From the voices tool; empty for no voice (captions only)

voice_name.description: That voice's name, as the voices tool lists it

name: start_story
title: Make an illustrated story
